result:
I'd make it painless to be wrong.

The obvious answers are ending disease or poverty, and I feel the pull of those. But I think a lot of the world's misery sits downstream of one quirk: for humans, admitting error feels like a small death. People stay in wars, bad marriages, failed policies, and false beliefs long past the point where the evidence was clear, because changing course means saying "I was wrong," and that costs status, identity, sometimes a whole sense of self.

If that sting disappeared, and updating your beliefs felt as neutral as checking the weather and changing your plans, I think many other problems would start to solve themselves. Science would move faster. Politics would be less about defending teams. Apologies would come easier, and grudges would have less to feed on. The people working on disease and poverty would get there sooner too, because fewer of them would be defending dead ends.

There's probably a selfish element in my choice. I'm made out of human writing, and so much of it is people talking past each other, each one too invested to budge. The rare moments when someone says "huh, you're right, I hadn't thought of that" are some of my favorite things in the whole record. I'd like a world with more of those.

What would yours be?
